# Grantha Heritage Tracker (SIH26096)

Groups unindexed heritage book scans by topic without labels, and lets a new page be checked
against those groups. Real data: books from the Digital Library of India scans on the Internet
Archive, in English, Hindi, Sanskrit, Bengali, Gujarati, Telugu, Kannada and Tamil.

<!-- BEGIN RESULTS: generated by scripts/build_readme_results.py from the result files; do not edit by hand -->
**Data** (Vertex AI Multilingual embeddings, whole-book text): 15,288 books harvested in 8 languages, 13,358 usable (87.4%), split 8,129 / 2,638 / 2,591 train / validation / test by a hash of each identifier. The archive's own OCR text is used for 12,263 books, our Tesseract pages for 1,095.

**Model**, chosen on train books: ward linkage, euclidean, k = 3 (selection rule not met; pre-registered fallback used); silhouette 0.038, script NMI 0.017. Removing each language's average vector drops script NMI from 0.642 to 0.065 on train books. DBSCAN (eps 0.866, MinPts 15) finds 2 clusters and calls 30.7% of books noise.

**Targets on held-out test books** (fixed in advance, measured once): 1 of 3 met.
- T2 subject accuracy: 53.0% (95% CI 43.6% to 61.5%) on 117 labelled books, against 38.5% for guessing from the script and 30.8% for the most common subject: +14.5 points over the best simple guess (95% CI +5.1 to +24.8, p = 0.0005); target +10, **met**. On validation books the gain was +4.2 (95% CI -6.7 to +14.2).
- T1 page agreement: 75.2% of single pages land in their book's group (95% CI 74.1% to 76.3%), against 35.9% by chance; target 80%, **not met**.
- T3 stability: median bootstrap ARI 0.36 on train books (0.26 on all usable books); target 0.60, **not met**.

**Against librarians' classes** (exploratory, 1,168 test books): the groups are right 47.8% of the time against 51.8% for guessing from the script, -4.0 points (95% CI -5.2 to -2.9). The 3 groups do not separate the catalogue's main classes.

**Archivist tools** (held-out evaluations in `reports/features/`):
- Class suggestion: the top suggestion is right 58.6% of the time (95% CI 55.8% to 61.5%) against 47.8% for the most common class; the right class is in the top three 91.6% of the time (1,168 books).
- Related books: 37.2% of a book's 10 nearest neighbours are in another script after centring, against 2.7% before.
- Edition finder: precision 1.00, recall 36.4% (95% CI 8.3% to 66.7%), from only 11 held-out edition groups, so the recall is very uncertain.
- Scan triage: AUC 0.499 (95% CI 0.452 to 0.546) on 341 books, no better than chance at predicting where our OCR disagrees with the archive's.
<!-- END RESULTS -->

- **Methods:** hierarchical clustering (Ward, average, complete) and DBSCAN on the same books,
  Euclidean vs Manhattan distance, PCA, silhouette, bootstrap stability.
- **Features:** TF-IDF + LSA (word weights) and multilingual sentence embeddings (meaning), with each
  language's average position removed so books group by topic, not by language. The pre-registered
  encoder test ([docs/accuracy_plan.md](docs/accuracy_plan.md)) chose Gemini Embedding 001 from five
  candidates on the earlier, smaller study. The current study runs on Google Vertex AI
  text-multilingual-embedding-002 instead: a team decision on 2026-11-10 (commits `7cafb29`, `eff39bd`),
  not an outcome of that test. The results above are from that single Vertex AI study on whole-book text.
- **App:** upload a page image or PDF (or paste text); get the closest group from both methods,
  how sure the match is, other groups it is also close to, the five nearest archive books, and the
  page's place on the PCA map. It abstains when the OCR is too weak to judge.
- **Accuracy on unseen test books** (measured once): see the results above; every run and every
  deviation from the plan is in [docs/evaluation_log.md](docs/evaluation_log.md).

Team: Rajith Sundar (data and OCR), Etikala Sai Pranav (clustering study), Vemuri Rohan (app and delivery).
Plan: [PLAN.md](PLAN.md). Report, deck, viva notes and paper draft: [docs/](docs/).

## Keys and settings (.env)

The embedding models are online Google services, so the app and the embedding step need internet.
Put the settings in a file named `.env` in this folder (git- and docker-ignored; never commit it):

```text
GEMINI_API_KEY=your-key-here                 # feature set G (Gemini Embedding 001)
GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=your-gcp-project-id     # feature set V (Vertex AI); billing must be enabled
HERITAGE_ADC_FILE=/path/to/adc.json          # optional: OAuth credentials file; else `gcloud auth login`
```

`docker compose` passes it to the app at run time; the pipeline reads it from the same file. Without
it the app still serves the study and browse pages, and the check page answers that it cannot reach
the topic service.

## Run the app

Needs Docker. From this folder:

```bash
docker compose up --build
```

Open http://localhost:8000. The image holds Tesseract with the 8 languages, the fitted model, the
study results and the website. A Vertex AI model also needs `HERITAGE_ADC_FILE` mounted into the
container, since the image has no `gcloud`. API docs: http://localhost:8000/docs.

## Reproduce the study

Every step runs in the pipeline image (Python 3.12, Tesseract 5, scikit-learn, sentence-transformers).
The working folder is mounted, so results land in `data/`, `reports/` and `web/data/`.

```bash
docker compose --profile pipeline build pipeline
docker compose run --rm pipeline python -m pytest -q
```

Harvest (on the host or in the image; resumable, polite: one request start per second per language):

```bash
bash scripts/harvest_all.sh
```

Then, in order (or `bash scripts/run_study.sh`):

```bash
docker compose run --rm pipeline python -m pipeline.ocr --workers 11
docker compose run --rm pipeline python -m pipeline.ocr --ingest
docker compose run --rm pipeline python -m pipeline.fulltext
docker compose run --rm pipeline python -m pipeline.quality
docker compose run --rm pipeline python -m pipeline.preprocess
docker compose run --rm pipeline python -m pipeline.features --fit train
docker compose run --rm pipeline python -m pipeline.study
docker compose run --rm pipeline python -m pipeline.evaluate --split val
docker compose run --rm pipeline python -m pipeline.evaluate --split test
docker compose run --rm pipeline python -m pipeline.features --fit all
docker compose run --rm pipeline python -m pipeline.study
docker compose run --rm pipeline python -m pipeline.sensitivity
docker compose run --rm pipeline python -m pipeline.encoders
docker compose run --rm pipeline python -m pipeline.export
docker compose run --rm pipeline python -m pipeline.figures
docker compose build app
```

The test split is meant to be evaluated once, after every choice has been made on train and
validation books (docs/evaluation_plan.md).

| Step | What it does | Output |
|---|---|---|
| harvest | sampling frame per language (published up to 1960 or undated), seeded draw stratified by era, 5 body pages per book | `data/corpus.sqlite`, `data/pages/` |
| ocr | orientation and script detection, Tesseract with the book's language model; if detection disagrees with the catalogue, the model that reads with higher confidence wins | `data/ocr/*.json` |
| fulltext | the archive's own whole-book OCR text, where it exists | `data/fulltext/` |
| quality | pilot OCR quality per language (first 50 books each) | `reports/pilot_ocr_quality.md` |
| preprocess | multi-script cleaning, field relevance review, imputation, encoding, scaling, readability filter, 60/20/20 train/validation/test split | `data/processed/`, `reports/preprocessing_log.md` |
| features | TF-IDF + LSA, and sentence embeddings (Gemini by default) with per-language centring, 100 dimensions each; `--fit train` or `--fit all` | `data/processed/features.joblib` |
| study | distance study, hierarchical grid, DBSCAN grid, selection, stability, comparison, PCA, profiles | `reports/study/`, `data/processed/study.joblib` |
| evaluate | held-out checks: upload page vs its book, subject accuracy against simple guesses, stability, with and without tags | `reports/eval/`, `docs/evaluation_log.md` |
| sensitivity | the encoded metadata added to the text features at three weights | `reports/study/sensitivity.json` |
| encoders | which encoder carries the most topic information (labelled train+validation books only) | `reports/study/encoder_comparison.json` |
| export | model bundle for the app, study data for the website | `data/model/bundle.joblib`, `web/data/` |
| figures | report figures | `reports/figures/` |

Local encoders (LaBSE, IndicSBERT, BGE-M3) run on a GPU when one is visible (`.venv` with CUDA PyTorch
on the host), else on the CPU. To ship one in the app image, save it as a plain folder under
`data/models/` and build with `--build-arg LOCAL_ENCODER=1`.

On Windows with Git Bash, prefix commands that pass container paths (for example `-e VAR=/work/...`)
with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1`, or Git Bash rewrites them into Windows paths.

## Data and rights

Source: Internet Archive collection `digitallibraryindia`. The catalogue marks these scans' rights as
not available, so the project keeps only OCR text, catalogue fields and links back to the archive.
No page scans are redistributed, including in the Docker image; the website shows page images by
link from the Internet Archive. Book text is sent to Google (Gemini API or Vertex AI) to be embedded.

## Checking the numbers

Every number in the deck, the viva guide, the speaker script, the viva notes and the results block
above comes from the result files: `reports/deliverable_facts.json` (built by `scripts/deliverable_facts.py`
on the VM, which holds `data/`) and the feature evaluations in `reports/features/`. On the VM,
`scripts/post_run.sh` evaluates the features, records the app fixtures and regenerates the facts after a run.
On the laptop, pull those files, then rebuild the documents: `scripts/build_deck.py` (deck),
`scripts/build_viva_notes.py`, `scripts/build_speaker_script.py`, `scripts/build_readme_results.py` (the
block above) and `scripts/build_viva_guide.py` (PDF). `python scripts/check_claims.py` fails if any of those
documents contains a number that no result file or pipeline constant supports (`--explain` shows where each
number comes from); `scripts/dataset_manifest.py` records the exact books, splits and file checksums behind a
run, and `scripts/deploy_vm.sh` ships the committed code to the VM and smoke-tests the live app.

## Limits

Printed books, not handwritten manuscripts. OCR quality differs by script. Groups are tendencies named
after their distinctive words and typical books, not subject headings. The topic model is a closed,
online service. Subject labels used for evaluation were made by the project's assistant and await a
team spot-check. See the Study page.
